headline: Histology and transcriptomics fused to reconstruct multiscale tissue architecture
label: Quantitative Imaging Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: Imaging and spatial transcriptomics are being coupled in computational frameworks that infer tissue structure from histology, scRNA-seq, and cell painting.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational extraction of quantitative tissue structure by coupling imaging-derived information with molecular profiles. Spatial transcriptomics methods (REMAP, Pixel2Gene, SpaMOAL, CellRefiner, stDyer-image) reconstruct or identify spatial organization by integrating scRNA-seq, co-registered histology, graph contrastive learning, or morphological image features. HRCHY-CytoCommunity infers nested, multi-level tissue structure from cell-type annotated spatial maps, and the CUBIC Organ/Body Atlas provides single-cell-resolution 3D references for eleven adult mouse organs. Imaging-centric items apply quantitative descriptors to cell painting and morphology: SCALE offers a configurable longitudinal cell painting pipeline, and a low-dose radiation study links RNA-seq predictors to nuclear morphology features. What is new is the coupling of imaging-derived quantities with transcriptomic frameworks, exemplified by SpaHE-Infil, which links spatial transcriptomics and H&E whole-slide images to infer 12 tumor microenvironment cell types.
